subject: Realtime API: degraded streaming performance in us-west-2 — immediate mitigations
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Kyle Morgan <kyle.morgan@harvestai.com>, Harvest AI Support <support@harvestai.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Realtime API: degraded streaming performance in us-west-2 — immediate mitigations

Hi Kyle —

We observed a degradation in streaming latencies for the Realtime API in us-west-2 starting ~08:50 PDT. Some client sessions saw chunk delivery latencies spike to 3–6s per chunk for sequences that normally finish <300ms. We believe this impacted a subset of streaming/chat connections rather than non-streaming generation.

Immediate steps we are taking now (short-term mitigation):
- Reverted a service-side routing tweak (adaptive-KV-routing v3) at 09:05 PDT — this reduced error rates but not all latency anomalies.
- Temporarily increased small-instance autoscaling in us-west-2 to absorb hotspot load (5x of baseline).
- Enabled relaxed batching on affected shards for sessions with prefix-cache miss, to reduce head-of-line blocking.

Customer-facing guidance you can apply right away:
- Shorten streaming recv timeout on client side to 6s and implement exponential backoff with jitter (helps avoid tight retries).
- Fallback to polling for endpoints that cannot tolerate intermittent multi-second chunk delays: call the non-streaming generate endpoint with the same model and poll at 1s intervals.
- If you can, pin shorter max_tokens per request (e.g., 256) so streaming chunks are smaller during the window.

I've attached a small diagnostics snapshot and a runbook fragment for the rollout rollback. We'll update this thread as we confirm the fix. Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts real-time UX.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Account Engineer, Redwood Inference

Kyle / Monica —

Quick technical note on mitigation and follow-up steps:
- Root cause (preliminary): we saw a hot shard in the kv-cache plane after v3 adaptive routing started favoring a small subset of nodes for long-running sessions. That produced a tail of cache misses and elevated per-chunk latency when the model runtime had to materialize KV pages from slower tier.
- Short-term: rollback of v3 routing is the right move (Monica confirmed), and we have a patch to add a micro-second backoff in the KV fetch path to avoid head-of-line blocking when multiple requests try to materialize the same page.
- Client guidance (adds to Monica's notes): enable streaming chunk buffering client-side (up to 3 chunks) and render progressively; set a 6s soft timeout per chunk and allow a single retry per chunk. If you use websocket ping/pong for liveness, increase ping interval to 30s during the incident window.

Planned postmortem and action items (we'll share a full RCA by EOD):
1) Hot-shard mitigation: improve balancing logic (INF-9981) — owner: Infra (ETA: 2029-05-21)
2) KV fetch path backoff & dedupe: deploy patch to runtime (owner: Runtime Eng) — ETA: 2029-05-17
3) Better telemetry: add sampling for per-chunk service time and a tail SLO alert (owner: Observability) — ETA: 2029-05-16
4) Customer playbook: update console guidance for streaming fallback & polling knob (owner: Solutions Eng / Monica) — ETA: 2029-05-15

I'll join a quick post-incident call if you want to run through the proposed fixes.

-Vivek

Subject: Post-incident summary: Realtime API streaming slowpath in us-west-2 (RCA & action items)

Kyle —

Thanks again for the quick coordination today. Below is a concise post-incident summary and the action items we committed to. This message contains the timeline, root cause (preliminary), customer mitigations, and the internal owner list for follow-ups.

Incident timeline (PDT):
- 08:50 — first customer reports of delayed streaming chunks via telemetry
- 08:55 — support escalation; Harvest engineering begins polling fallback
- 09:05 — Redwood rollback of adaptive-KV-routing v3; partial improvement observed
- 10:15 — warmed additional instances + increased small-instance autoscale; chunk latencies returned to baseline for most sessions
- 12:00 — runtime patch (backoff + dedupe) staged to canary; verified no regression on canary traffic
- 16:30 — patch promoted to production in us-west-2; monitoring shows tail latency SLO restored

Root cause (summary):
- A routing change intended to reduce cross-host KV traffic concentrated long-lived sessions onto a small host subset. That caused cache hot-spotting and a tail of KV fetches that forced the runtime into a slowpath for affected sequences.

Customer mitigations already shared:
- Polling fallback, reduced max_tokens per request, recv-timeout=6s, single-chunk retry, client-side chunk buffering, increase websocket ping interval to 30s.

Action items (owner — ETA):
- Infra: implement adaptive balancing thresholds to prevent node concentration (Markus Klein) — ETA: 2029-05-21
- Runtime Eng: finalize KV fetch dedupe/backoff and land patch (owner: Runtime Eng team) — ETA: 2029-05-17
- Observability: add per-chunk tail SLO alert and dashboard tile; create incident runbook checklist (owner: Laura Bennett) — ETA: 2029-05-16
- Solutions/Docs: update customer console guidance and public KB with explicit fallback examples (owner: Monica Patel) — ETA: 2029-05-15

We will produce a full RCA doc and share it in the Drive link (included above) and update the Jira INF-9981 with the technical implementation details. If you want a walk-through of the patch behavior and the client knobs, Vivek and I can schedule a 30 minute session this week.

Apologies again for the disruption — we appreciate your patience and the quick mitigations on your side.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai
